intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that split-hand/foot malformation-6 (SHFM6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene on chromosome 12q13.

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation-6 (SHFM6) is caused by homozygous mutation in the WNT10B gene.
checks.evidence_quote: a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation (p.R332W) in all affected individuals but the atypical case plus in an asymptomatic female
checks.explanation: The paper reports a homozygous WNT10b mutation as the first recessive mutation in SHFM. 'SHFM6' is OMIM's name for the condition.

checks.claim: The WNT10B gene is located on chromosome 12q13.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified by homozygosity mapping a novel SHFM locus at 12q13.11-q13 with a maximum multipoint lod score of 5.47 and by subsequent candidate gene approach a homozygous missense WNT10b mutation
checks.explanation: WNT10b was found by a candidate gene search within the 12q13 locus. The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a limb malformation affecting the central rays of the hands and/or feet, characterized by absence of the central digital rays, a deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits (Gul and Oktenli, 2002; Blattner et al., 2010). Most familial cases are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner (Gul and Oktenli, 2002); SHFM6 is the autosomal recessive form associated with mutation in WNT10B (Ugur and Tolun, 2008; Blattner et al., 2010).

checks.claim: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a limb malformation affecting the central rays of the hands and/or feet.
checks.evidence_quote: Split-hand/foot malformation (SHFM) is a limb malformation affecting the central rays of the hands and/or feet.

checks.claim: SHFM is characterized by absence of the central digital rays, a deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits.
checks.evidence_quote: is characterized by the absence of the central digital rays, deep median cleft, and syndactyly of the remaining digits.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this almost word for word.

checks.claim: Most familial cases of SHFM are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.
checks.evidence_quote: The majority of the familial cases are inherited in an autosomal dominant manner.

checks.claim: SHFM6 is the autosomal recessive form of SHFM associated with mutation in WNT10B.
checks.evidence_quote: This is the first reported WNT10b mutation on the pathogenesis of limb development and recessive mutation in SHFM.
checks.explanation: The paper describes a recessive WNT10B mutation in autosomal recessive SHFM.

paragraphs.text: Verma et al. (1976) concluded that their consanguineous family, together with the reports of Ray and Freire-Maia (1971), demonstrated that split-hand and split-foot deformity can be inherited as an autosomal recessive trait. Mufti and Wood (1987) considered an autosomal recessive gene the likely mode of inheritance in their family. Zlotogora and Nubani (1989) and Gul and Oktenli (2002) discussed both autosomal recessive inheritance and a 2-locus model; in the 2-locus model proposed by Zlotogora and Nubani (1989), a dominant mutation at a controlling locus leads to nonpenetrance of a dominant SHFM mutation.

paragraphs.text: Homozygous WNT10B mutations were identified in a consanguineous kindred with autosomal recessive SHFM (Ugur and Tolun, 2008), in which the authors proposed either a contributing second locus or a suppressor locus, and in a patient with sporadic SHFM whose 9 heterozygous relatives showed no sign of SHFM (Blattner et al., 2010). Blattner et al. (2010) concluded that sporadic SHFM is not always a dominant trait and may carry a 25% recurrence risk for sibs.

agent.process_note: All 11 files opened; none had full text (3 title only, 8 abstract only). The causal gene (WNT10B, homozygous) and the 12q13.11-q13 locus came from Ugur and Tolun (2008), Blattner et al. (2010) and Kantaputra et al. (2018). No gene MIM number was supplied, so none was written. The abstracts lack: the nucleotide change for R332W; the exact nucleotide/protein designation, ancestry and consanguinity for the Blattner 4-bp duplication; and ancestry for most families. Elliott and Evans (2006) is a general SHFM genotype-phenotype abstract and was left uncited.
